technology.summary:
Today's technology news includes the announcement of Microsoft's new AI chip, the Maia 300, which will make the company less reliant on Nvidia's GPUs. Amazon has over 1 million robot workers, which raises questions about the future of human employees. A former Plaud executive has raised $26 million for an AI app that listens to users in the background. The Fitbit Edge has been officially announced, offering a compromise between smartwatches and screenless fitness trackers.

Other news includes a TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 event focused on building enduring companies in the AI era, an article on learning to use local AI, and an analysis of why the LeapPad couldn't survive the iPad. Additionally, Apple's upcoming "Welcome Home" event is expected to feature smart home-related announcements, including refreshes to Apple TV and HomePod Mini, and possibly a new platform called homeOS.

finance.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has teamed up with the Reserve Bank of India to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. However, high crude oil prices, increasing bond yields, and continued foreign selling are impacting the market and investor sentiment. A resurgent El Niño pattern could also deepen a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, pushing yields higher. Meanwhile, Indian equity benchmarks have experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices.

politics.summary:
The Delhi High Court has dismissed pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. The Supreme Court is to list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Jairam Ramesh has attacked the CEC, claiming his ability to execute illegal orders makes him a liability for the country. Meanwhile, Donald Trump has called the US electoral process 'corrupt', citing an Indian election that didn't happen.

In other news, Koel Mallick has joined the BJP, and India's foreign exchange reserves have reportedly declined by USD 18.34 billion in a single week.
